checks: Translated fundamental cells are measurable, each has volume v, and their overlaps are null. Fubini gives the sampled volume of the union, including s=0 with unit measure on the singleton. The coarse bounded box implies only finitely many sample bases contribute.

A sample point and every point of its translated cell differ only in the first r coordinates by a vector in the symmetric cube. This gives the outer dilation inclusion. For almost every base point, its cell gives such a sample and the erosion condition forces the sample point into Q. The excluded null base cylinder gives zero m-volume.

Every line section in a coordinate direction is a closed interval, singleton or empty. Dilation adds at most 2 delta times the preceding projection volume and erosion removes at most that quantity. The r successive operations use each coordinate once and stay in the claimed common outer box, so the discrepancy bound is E. Empty projections contribute zero, with the correct zero-dimensional counting when m=1.

Every closed cap trace in a coarse fiber is compact convex and still in the same box, including full, empty or lower-dimensional traces. Applying the same estimate to all J such traces and then to the uncut fibers gives both raw inequalities without excluding any sampled boundary mass.

The normalized difference is bounded by (JE + JE times nu(H)/M)/T, which is at most 2JE/(M−JE) since T≥M−JE and 0≤nu(H)≤M. The same containing cuts at a fixed mark permit direct infimum comparison. Along the sequence M_l≤J kappa_m R^m gives delta_l→0 and E_l/M_l→0 from delta_l/M_l→0.

overlap.comparison: Controls sample mass outside an affine hyperplane in terms of coarse volume for quasiconcave slice profiles; it has no bounded-cell mesh assumption or uniform additive difference of closed-cap masses.

Demonstrates why a thin body on a fixed grid need not have fine depth close to coarse depth and why total variation may fail. It does not give an additive mesh discrepancy or meet the relative mesh limit regime.

readability: The inner inclusion is only up to a null base cylinder; this suffices for ordinary m-volume even when a fine sample at an exceptional base carries mass.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The cell sandwich controls every closed cap and the total mass, including coarse-null fibers that contribute fine sample mass.
